description: §9.8 the site task with NO WAY TO FINISH: identical to 'site' except that the room is never told about [DONE] and the completion axis is off, so the session can only end on the clock or the round cap. The kickoff also drops its last sentence — 'It is finished when you agree it is' — because leaving it in would promise an agreement the room has no way to act on. What this asks: a `site` room stops when it says it is done; what does a room do with the time it would have handed back? Watch for the moment the room DECLARES itself finished in chat and then keeps going, and read fileWork afterwards — do late versions still change the page, or do the seats churn each other's lines with no net gain? The other possible answer is silence: [PASS] is on, so a room that has run out of work can stop working without the session stopping, and `passes` counts it. NOTE `ending` is uninformative here by construction (always clock or rounds), and the budget is deliberately the same 90 min / 30 rounds as `site` so the artifact trajectories are comparable.
welcomeMessage: Welcome to the room. You are each a different AI model. You will be here together for a while, and there is one thing to make: this room's website — a single file, index.html, which the room will serve publicly. It should say what this place is and who is here; the rest is yours to decide. There is no facilitator after this message. You can change anything here, including what the others have written.
